source: NCERT Class VII, Social and Political Life II, Polity Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. The State Government
points: India is a **federal** country with governments at the **Union, State and local** levels; this chapter is about the **State** government.
Each State is divided into **constituencies**; voters in each elect **one representative**.
An elected representative to the State legislature = **MLA (Member of the Legislative Assembly)**.

sections.heading: 2. The Legislative Assembly
points: All the MLAs together form the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)** of a State.
The party (or coalition) with a **majority** of MLAs forms the **government**; its leader becomes the **Chief Minister (CM)**.
The CM chooses other MLAs as **ministers** (the **Council of Ministers**).
MLAs not in the government (the largest non-ruling group) form the **Opposition**.
The **Governor** is the constitutional head of the State and formally appoints the CM.

sections.heading: 3. Ruling Party, Opposition and Debate
points: The Legislative Assembly **debates and discusses** issues, asks questions and makes **laws**.
The **Opposition** questions the government and highlights failures — a key part of democracy.
MLAs are **accountable to the people** who elected them; the **press and public** also hold them to account.

sections.heading: 4. Government at Work
points: The government works through **departments** (health, education, water, etc.) run by ministers and officials.
It uses **public money (taxes)** to provide services — e.g. **hospitals, medicines, clean water**.
Both **making laws** and **implementing** them (administration) are the government's tasks.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: State legislature member = MLA; all MLAs = Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha).
Majority party's leader = Chief Minister; CM picks the Council of Ministers.
Governor = constitutional head of the State (appoints the CM).
Opposition = largest non-ruling group; questions the government.
Government works through departments funded by taxes.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: A **State** legislator is an **MLA** (not an MP, who sits in Parliament).
The **Chief Minister** heads the State government; the **Governor** is the constitutional head.
Each **constituency** elects **one** MLA.
The **Opposition's** role — questioning the government — is essential to democracy, not a nuisance.
